THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

This petition by the plaintiffs is directed against the impugned order dated 19.06.2023 whereby the application I.A.No.34 filed by the petitioner-plaintiff under Order 16 Rule 1 & 2, CPC seeking permission to adduce additional evidence to examine witnesses whose names were not contained in the list of witnesses was partly allowed by the Trial Court by permitting the petitioner-plaintiff to examine one witness No.3 and rejecting the request of the plaintiff to examine witnesses Nos.1 & 2.
2.
A perusal of the material on record will indicate that the petitioner-plaintiff instituted the aforesaid suit against the respondents-defendants, who are contesting the suit.
The plaintiff having examined himself as PW.1 was cross examined by the respondents-defendants and the matter was posted for evidence of defendants.

At that stage, petitioner-plaintiff filed the instant NC:
2024:KHC:9932 application I.A.No.34 for permission to examine 3 witnesses and I.A.No.35 to reopen the case for permission to adduce further evidence.

The details of the 3 witnesses sought to be examined by the petitioner-plaintiff are as under:
 SI. Details of the Witnesses  No.
1. Office of the Sub Registrar and Marriage Registration Officer, Rajajinagar (Yeshwanthpur), 1 ^
(st) Floor, 3B Complex, No.199, 13th Cross, 2nd Stage, West of Chord Road, Bangalore - 560086.
Purpose: To produce the Gazette Notification indicating the Guideline Value of the Properties / Sites carved out of Re. Sy.No. 190, old Sy. No. 172 (Sy.No.170) of Kethamaranahalli Village,
Yeshwanthapura Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk, now lying in West of Chord Road, 2 ^ (nd) Stage,
2nd Phase Layout (near Nandini Talkies), Bangalore, and the surrounding area falling within the said Notification, for the period from 24.3.1990 till date.

3. Special Land Acquisition Officer (Bangalore West), Bangalore Development Authority, Land Acquisition Department, Kumara Park West, T.Chowdaiah Road, Bangalore 560020.

Purpose: The witness to produce and depose regarding the documents relating to acquisition of Re.

No. 172 (Sy.No.170) of Kethamaranahalli Village, Yeshwanthapura Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk, for taking possession and demolition of structures put-up on the said property.

The witness to depose regarding the disbursement of compensation and the litigations before various Courts involving Bangalore Development Authority with respect to Re. Sy.No. 190, old Sy. No. 172 (Sy.No.170) of Kethamaranahalli Village, Yeshwanthapura Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk.

3. The said application having been opposed by the respondents-defendants, the Trial Court allowed I.A.No.35 in full and partly allowed I.A.No.34 and permitted the petitioner-plaintiff to examine the SLAO - BDA (additional witness No.3).

However the request of the petitioner to examine Sub-Registrar and Sri Madhusudhan Wadhwani as two additional witnesses was rejected by the Trial Court, which disallowed I.A.No.34 to the said extent by passing the impugned order which is assailed in the present petition.
4. A perusal of the order dated 09.03.2023 passed by this Court in MFA No.1491/2023 will indicate that the Trial Court has been directed to dispose of the suit expeditiously.

Under these circumstances, in order to facilitate expeditious disposal of not only NC: 2024:KHC:9932 the present petition but also the suit, this Court passed the following order on 05.03.2024, which reads as under:
"Petitioner is permitted to implead the Sub Registrar and Marriage Registration Officer, Rajajinagar (Yeshwanthpur), 1st Floor, 3B Complex, No.199, 13th Cross, 2nd Stage, West of Chord Road, Bangalore - 560086, as additional respondent No.6 to the petition.
Petitioner is permitted to carry out the amendment and file the amended cause title by the next date of hearing.

sentences.text: Smt. M.V.Adithi, learned AGA is directed to accept notice for impleading additional respondent No.6.
Re-list on 11.03.2024 under the caption 'Orders'.
Interim order granted earlier is extended till the next date of hearing."

5. In pursuance of the same, learned AGA appearing on behalf of additional respondent No.6 who is cited as witness No.1, the Sub-Registrar as stated supra, submits that the said Sub Registrar would be physically present before the Trial Court on the next date of hearing of the suit i.e., on 18.03.2024 and produce the documents as sought for in the application and also give evidence in this regard.

So also the learned counsel for the petitioner submits that insofar as additional witness No.2 - Sri Madhusudhan NC: 2024:KHC:9932 Wadhwani is concerned, the petitioner would keep the said witnesses personally present without insisting on issuance of witness summons with the said witness.
It is therefore submitted that the impugned order passed by the Trial Court deserves to be set aside and I.A.No.34 deserves to be allowed in full as sought for by the petitioner.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for contesting private respondents in addition to supporting the impugned order submits that it is always open for the petitioner to obtain certified copies of the documents sought to be summoned from the Sub Registrar.
It is submitted that the evidence of additional witness No.2 is neither relevant nor material for the purpose of adjudication of the issues in controversy between the parties.

It is also submitted that the petitioner is unnecessarily protracting the matter despite the directions issued by this Court and as such the Trial Court was fully justified in partly rejecting the instant application I.A.No.34 in part by passing the impugned order which does not warrant interference by this Court in the present petition.
7.
It is true that the directions issued by this Court for the purpose of disposal of the suit has already expired as on today.

However, having regard to the rival contentions between the parties coupled with the fact that the evidentiary value / probative value of the additional evidence sought to be adduced by the petitioner-plaintiff would have to be appreciated at the time of final arguments, I am of the view that the Trial Court has committed an error in pre-judging the entire issue and refusing to permit the petitioner-plaintiff to produce additional evidence of additional witnesses 1 and 2.

It is also relevant to state that in the light of the submissions made by the learned AGA that the Jurisdictional Sub Registrar who is cited as witness No.1 would be present before the Trial Court on 18.03.2024 and the respondents would be entitled to cross-examine the said witnesses with reference to his oral and documentary evidence, I am of the view that no prejudice to be caused to the respondents if petitioner is permitted to adduce the additional evidence of witness no.1.
8.

Insofar as additional witness No.2 - Sri Madhusudhan Wadhwani is concerned, the respondents would be entitled to cross-examine the said witnesses also and on this score also, no prejudice can be said to have been caused to the respondents- NC: 2024:KHC:9932 defendants if the petitioner to adduce further evidence of said witness also.

5 9.

sentences.text: A perusal of the impugned order will indicate that the Trial Court has not assigned proper or cogent reasons as to why the evidence of additional witnesses 1 and 2 is not required and the impugned order has occasioned failure of justice warranting interference of this Court in the present petition.

As stated supra, since the respondents would be entitled to cross-examine the additional witnesses, it cannot be said that any prejudice would be caused to the respondents, if the petitioner-plaintiff is permitted to adduce further evidence.

10. In the result, I pass the following:-
ORDER (i) The petition is hereby allowed.
(ii) The impugned order dated 19.06.2023 passed in O.S.No.4707/2010 insofar as it relates to rejecting I.A.No.34 in part is hereby set aside.
(iii) Both I.A.Nos.34 and 35 filed by the petitioner-plaintiff are allowed in full.
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:9932 (iv) The Jurisdictional Sub-Registrar (Addl. Impleaded respondent No.6) is directed to appear before the Trial Court on 18.03.2024.
(v) The petitioner is permitted to examine Sri Madhusudhan Wadhwani as additional witness in the suit by bringing him personally without seeking issuance of witness summons to the said witnesses.
(vi) Liberty is reserved in favour of both parties to examine / cross-examine the said additional two witnesses.
(vii) In view of the disposal of this petition, the time stipulated for disposal of the suit is extended up to 20.12.2024.
(viii) The Trial Court is directed to provide sufficient and reasonable opportunity to the respondents to cross-examine the additional two witnesses.

SD/-
